draft.title: Reading motion from graphs
card: Displacement-time
the gradient at a point is the velocity. A horizontal tangent means velocity is 0, so the particle is at rest at that moment.
Velocity-time
the height of the graph is the velocity. Where it touches or crosses the t-axis, the velocity is 0. The gradient of this graph is the acceleration.
Changing direction
the velocity must change sign. On a velocity-time graph, the graph crosses the t-axis. On a displacement-time graph, the curve turns at a peak or a trough.
Speeding up
the particle speeds up when velocity and acceleration have the same sign, and slows down when the signs differ. Example: v = −3 and a = −2 means speeding up.
draft.remember: Rest means v = 0. A change of direction needs v to change sign. Same signs for v and a mean speeding up.

a.q: On a velocity-time graph, a particle's graph crosses the t-axis from above to below at t = 4. What happens at t = 4?
opts: It stops and then continues the same way
a.why: Crossing the t-axis means velocity changes from positive to negative, so the particle reverses direction. Touching the axis without crossing would give rest with no change of direction, which is the tempting wrong idea.
a.clue: Look at the sign of velocity before and after t = 4.

b.q: At t = 2 a particle has velocity −3 m/s and acceleration −2 m/s². What is the particle doing at that moment?
b.why: Velocity is negative, so the particle moves backwards. Velocity and acceleration have the same sign, so the speed is increasing. Negative acceleration alone does not mean slowing down.
b.clue: Compare the signs of velocity and acceleration.

problems.detail: Question b uses exactly the card's worked example (v = −3, a = −2, speeding up), so students can match it from memory without applying the idea. Different values would test understanding.

The options use 'forwards' and 'backwards', but the card never says that negative velocity means moving in the negative (backwards) direction. Half of the answer depends on a convention the card does not state.

check.summary: The card and both answers are correct. Question b copies the card's own example word for word, and it relies on 'negative velocity means backwards', which the card never states.

proposal.title: Reading motion from graphs
card: Displacement-time
the gradient at a point is the velocity. A horizontal tangent means velocity is 0, so the particle is at rest at that moment.
Velocity-time
the height of the graph is the velocity, and its gradient is the acceleration. Above the t-axis the particle moves in the positive direction. Below it, the particle moves in the negative direction.
Changing direction
the velocity must change sign. On a velocity-time graph, the graph crosses the t-axis. On a displacement-time graph, the curve turns at a peak or a trough.
Speeding up
the particle speeds up when velocity and acceleration have the same sign, and slows down when the signs differ. Example: v = −3 and a = −2 means speeding up.
proposal.remember: Rest means v = 0. A change of direction needs v to change sign. Same signs for v and a mean speeding up.

a.q: On a velocity-time graph, a particle's graph crosses the t-axis from above to below at t = 4. What happens at t = 4?
opts: It stops and then continues the same way
a.why: Crossing the t-axis means velocity changes from positive to negative, so the particle reverses direction. Stopping and carrying on the same way would need the graph to touch the axis without crossing, so velocity would not change sign.
a.clue: Look at the sign of velocity before and after t = 4.

b.q: At t = 3, a particle's velocity-time graph is above the t-axis and sloping downwards. What is the particle doing at that moment?
opts: Moving in the positive direction and slowing down
Moving in the positive direction and speeding up
Moving in the negative direction and slowing down
Moving in the negative direction and speeding up
b.why: The graph is above the t-axis, so velocity is positive and the particle moves in the positive direction. The downward slope means the acceleration is negative, so the signs differ and the particle slows down. A downward slope does not mean moving in the negative direction: that depends on which side of the t-axis the graph is.
b.clue: Height gives the velocity's sign. Gradient gives the acceleration's sign.

b.best: Moving in the positive direction and slowing down
